digest.component_or_area: MCP error surface and CLI error code emission
propositions: MCP tool failures currently arrive as unstructured prose in exception messages or ad-hoc partial shapes, whereas the CLI emits a structured `error_envelope` discriminator; MCP must emit the same discriminator sourced from a single shared vocabulary to allow agents to distinguish failure types.

No central classifier exists; error codes are scattered literal strings across 12 CLI emission sites and the library exposes no machine error identity, so a three-way cross-interface test (library, CLI, MCP) has no value to compare against.

Two MCP tools already emit divergent ad-hoc partial shapes (`_mcp_reads.py` returns `{error, kind}`; `_mcp_llm.py` returns `{error, ...}`) that must be migrated to the envelope while preserving agent-branching fields (`kind`, `resolution_class`, `retryable`, `diagnostic`).

The read facade flattens `TicketNotFoundError` into a generic `RebarError`, so the new classifier must either preserve subclass identity to the MCP boundary or attach an `error_code` attribute to the flattened exception.

A held-out test must pin each emitted code so rewording the human message cannot change the machine `error` identity, and a cross-interface test must verify the library `error_code_for`, CLI envelope, and MCP envelope all emit an identical code for the same failure.
